items.title: A pencil on a nonsingular proper curve gives either a map of degree at most d or a trivial map with nontrivial global functions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file curves.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma dichotomizes the map defined by a pencil (statement lines 626-636). The proof (lines 638-658) is complete: the degree bounds from the nonzero map, the triviality case with its global-functions consequence, and the nonconstant case with the degree formula and O(1) of degree one. Every step is present with no omissions. H2: a short case split with standard degree bookkeeping.
